    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    Nevada has over 300 geothermal sites, ranging from rugged, remote desert soaking pools to historic commercial mineral Carson Hot Springs. 
    Best Natural & Primitive Hot Springs
    • Spencer Hot Springs (Austin): Located in the Big Smoky Valley, these free Bureau of Land Management (BLM) metal cowboy tubs and natural mud pools sit at 90–110°F with sweeping mountain views and visiting wild burros. 
    • Gold Strike Hot Springs (Boulder City): A thrilling and strenuous 2.5-mile slot-canyon hike near the Hoover Dam featuring boulder scrambles, rope climbs, and multiple steamy pools averaging 100–109°F along the Colorado River (open October through May). 
    • Ruby Valley Hot Springs (Elko): A remote, crystal-clear emerald natural pool sitting around 100–103°F
      in the middle of open marshland. High-clearance or 4WD vehicles are recommended for the dirt roads.
       
    • Fish Lake Valley Hot Well (Dyer): A county-managed geothermal pipe and tub system near the California border overflowing into warm goldfish ponds, featuring a vault toilet and free dispersed camping. 
    • Soldier Meadows Hot Springs (Gerlach): Found deep in the Black Rock Desert region, this natural hot creek features rock-dammed pools ranging from 90–112°F alongside primitive BLM campgrounds. 
    Best Commercial Resorts & Spas
    Carson Hot Springs (Carson City): Operating since 1849, this historic site offers four large outdoor open-air mineral pools and ten private indoor clawfoot tubs filled with natural 98°F mineral water. 
    David Walley's Resort (Genoa): Tucked against the Sierra Nevada foothills, this upscale retreat features five outdoor mineral-infused pools heated between 98–104°F, a full-service spa, and an on-site restaurant. 
    Steamboat Hot Springs Healing Center & Spa (Reno): Named by Mark Twain in 1863, this historic wellness center offers private indoor and outdoor mineral baths, steam rooms, and therapeutic treatments. 
    Are you looking for a primitive backcountry adventure or a relaxing resort with amenities, and which part of Nevada will you be visiting?
